2610.12837.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
2610.12837.paper_summary: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.
2610.12837.paper_summary_zh: 知識蒸餾旨在訓練一個較小的學生模型，以模仿在資源受限環境中較大的教師模型。<lb/>然而，蒸餾過程通常是數據密集且計算成本高，特別是在生成任務中。<lb/>少樣本蒸餾提供了一種替代方案，通過使用有限的訓練樣本轉移教師知識。<lb/>然而，我們觀察到，少樣本蒸餾的性能在很大程度上依賴於這些訓練樣本的選擇。<lb/>事實上，我們證明了使用更不確定的樣本，特別是在教師的決策邊界附近，會顯著惡化蒸餾性能。<lb/>受到這一觀察的啟發，我們提出了在開放書籍問答中的反事實引導少樣本蒸餾（COFFEQA），這是一種新穎的策略，恰當地利用反事實來提供對具有挑戰性的事實樣本的額外監督。<lb/>在生成問答設置中，我們將反事實定義為一個最小修改的上下文，這會促使教師改變其對替代答案的回應。<lb/>我們提供幾何見解，說明事實-反事實對如何約束教師和學生的決策邊界之間的偏差。<lb/>我們進一步介紹了一個新的指標，即上下文跟隨難度（CFD），該指標在蒸餾之前根據與預期替代答案的一致性和對修改上下文的依賴性進一步驗證反事實。<lb/>COFFEQA 使用 CFD 驗證過的事實-反事實對進行少樣本蒸餾。<lb/>在五個領域內和三個領域外的問答基準上進行的實驗，使用 T5 和 Qwen2.5 系列顯示，COFFEQA 在相同的少樣本預算下超越了僅使用事實的蒸餾基準。<lb/>例如，在 TriviaQA 上，COFFEQA 在 T5 設置下以 32 個少樣本對的情況下，平均提高了 8.77 個 EM 點和 9.98 個 F1 點，相較於僅使用事實的基準。
